chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said:

'Ali, the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), entered a graveyard with his companions and called out: O people of the dust! O people of loneliness! O people of quietness! O people of stillness! As for the news we have, as for your wealth, it has been distributed, and your women have been remarried, and your houses have been occupied. So what is the news with you? Then he turned to his companions and said: By Allah, if they were permitted to speak, they would have said, 'No provision is like piety. The best provision is piety.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Belieathers (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to the dead in the graveyard regarding their worldly possessions and piety?
ai.summary: In this poignant narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Ali (a.s.) addresses the deceased with rhetorical questions highlighting the transience of worldly possessions—wealth, spouses, and homes—which are left behind for the living. He concludes that if the dead could speak, they would testify that piety (*Taqwa*) is the ultimate provision (*Zad*) for the journey to the Hereafter. This scene underscores the Shia emphasis on *Ziyarat* as a moment of reflection on mortality and the spiritual preparation required for the afterlife.
